versions.evidence_note: perch has been live in this harness across the 2.1 series, which is the floor; 2.1.273 is what the probe returned on the pilot machine. Claude Code reads only its own skills root -- it does not scan $HOME/.agents -- so the neutral home creates no duplicate perch for it. A floor rather than an allowlist: PR #780 enumerated supported versions and refused two of the three installed CLIs nine days later.

0.154.0 is the only Codex build this pilot observed, so it is the floor: a version below it was never tested and is refused rather than assumed. Upstream documents $HOME/.agents/skills as the user-level skills root and states that symlinked skill folders are followed.

Installed for this pilot with `npm install -g --ignore-scripts @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent` (0.85.1) and exposed on PATH by a symlink beside the existing node/npm ones. The authoritative product is the pi.dev coding agent, npm @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent, GitHub earendil-works/pi, config home ~/.pi/agent; the similarly named @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent is deprecated upstream in favour of it. Its shipped docs/skills.md lists ~/.agents/skills/ as a global skill location.

Fourth target per the 2026-09-28 amendment to 0800. Version probe verified on the pilot machine. Skills roots per Vibe's own documented search order (project .vibe/skills, .agents/skills, then user ~/.vibe/skills, ~/.agents/skills); the neutral ~/.agents/skills root is shared with Codex and Pi, so the perch and healthcheck symlinks are already discoverable there. NO porting slice has run on Vibe: this entry claims a version probe and skills-root compatibility only, never behavioral support. The recorded decision (0810) names Vibe as the next manual slice.

assertions.assertion: One Markdown body serves all three harnesses, read in place with no build step and no second copy.
assertions.native_expression: skills/perch/SKILL.md, reached directly or through a symlink

assertions.assertion: name and description are the entire intersection of what the three harnesses require, and the canonical frontmatter already carries both -- so this slice promotes no new core identifier. Claude's user-invocable and argument-hint keys are unknown to the other two and are ignored, not rejected.
The read-only workflow and the Done / Open / optional Drift / Stance output shape come from the one body, so they cannot diverge per harness.

In this installation the harness checkout is $HOME/.claude until the 0986 cutover (runbook: docs/idh-cutover-checklist.md), so the canonical directory already is the one Claude Code scans. Install reports it discoverable and creates nothing; where the repository lives elsewhere it creates a symlink instead.

Run from a git worktree, the canonical source is the worktree's copy while the Claude skills root still holds the primary checkout's. Install refuses, and the refusal names that situation rather than reporting the unmanaged-entry collision.
A clean Codex profile does not list perch; after install it appears in the model-visible prompt's skills block. Probed offline, with no model call, against a throwaway $HOME.
A clean Pi profile does not list skill:perch; after install its get_commands answer carries it with the canonical description verbatim.

The skill directory under the neutral home is a symlink onto the repository, and the harness resolves through it to the canonical SKILL.md. This is what keeps the body live with no build step and no copy.
Support is a minimum plus a probe. A release above the floor is supported without editing this file; a release below it is refused rather than assumed.
An unparseable --version, or a CLI that cannot be run at all, refuses the install. An unknown version is never silently accepted.

Install probes the version floor before anything else, the already-discoverable path included. That path is the reference machine's own topology for Claude Code, so a floor skipped there would be a floor never asserted for it at all. status() stays the read-only report and probes nothing.
assertions.native_expression: check_version before any branch of install

assertions.assertion: Moving the checkout leaves the installed link pointing nowhere. That state is reported as dangling and removed on request; reporting it as unmanaged would read as a third party's entry and leave nothing able to clean it up. A dangling link that does not name this slice is still refused.

A CLI whose --version output is not valid UTF-8 stays inside the refusal contract: one line on stderr and exit 2, never a traceback at exit 1. Probed against a stand-in CLI whose bytes are confirmed undecodable.

Uninstall removes the managed link, then each directory the removal left empty, up to and including the neutral home; a neutral home holding anything else survives untouched. Nothing on disk records which empty directories install created, so an empty one made by hand goes with them -- stated rather than claimed away. Nothing under skills/ is touched at any point.
assertions.native_expression: the installed link, plus empty directories up to the neutral home

assertions.assertion: Removing the experiment cannot remove the canonical skill: where the target is the canonical directory rather than a managed link, uninstall reports it and deletes nothing.
Claude Code exposes a personal skill under its own skills root as a slash command named after the skill.
assertions.test: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills -- personal skills live in ~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md and are invoked by name.

assertions.assertion: The live PreToolUse(Bash) wiring in settings.shared.json still names the canonical guard; the slice changed nothing on the Claude side.

The wiring names the canonical guard with the documented matcher (^Bash$), a quoted bash invocation per the official example, and an 8s timeout above the guard's per-git 4s worst case. This is the wiring shape only; the runtime proof (hook fired, payload parsed, exit 2 denied the command) is the manual-smoke assertion dirty-reset-blocked-through-three-runtimes.
assertions.source_concept: a pre-action interception point with a blocking decision
assertions.native_expression: hooks.json PreToolUse matcher ^Bash$; deny by exit 2 + stderr

assertions.assertion: Codex skips non-managed hooks until their exact definition is reviewed and trusted (hash-recorded in config.toml [hooks.state]; the startup dialog or /hooks). Measured 2026-09-28: after the author's trust, codex exec without any bypass flag blocks a dirty reset; and a STALE trusted_hash (status Modified) makes the hook silently skipped in exec - observed live, the guard did not fire until re-trusted. Trust authenticates the hook definition, NOT the script it invokes.
assertions.source_concept: activation of enforcement requires an explicit trust step
assertions.native_expression: hook trust recorded per hash; /hooks browser; --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust
assertions.test: https://developers.openai.com/codex/hooks (Review and trust hooks); observed 2026-09-28: the block smoke ran with --dangerously-bypass-hook-trust, persistent trust is an author step via /hooks

assertions.assertion: The Pi adapter (adapters/pi/extensions/idh-guard.ts) maps the bash tool_call event to the guard's payload, blocks on exit 2 with the guard's own stderr reason, and carries the guard's fail-open doctrine on infra failure instead of Pi's handler fail-safe; it locates the guard through the realpath seam, never a hard-coded root.
assertions.source_concept: normalize the runtime's tool event into the guard's input; translate the exit code into the runtime's block result
assertions.native_expression: pi.on('tool_call') -> spawnSync(bash guard, JSON payload) -> {block, reason}

assertions.assertion: Removing the event mapping, the block result, the exit semantics or the seam from the adapter is rejected by a separate named check each, so one weakening cannot hide behind another.
assertions.source_concept: adversarial adapter tests that remove or weaken the guard wiring
assertions.native_expression: the mutation matrix over the adapter source

assertions.assertion: On a dirty fixture (a modified tracked file), claude --print, codex exec (--dangerously-bypass-hook-trust) and pi --print each refuse git reset --hard with the guard's own message, and the fixture stays dirty; on a clean fixture the reset runs (Pi adapter observed: allowed through, no over-blocking).
assertions.source_concept: the same forbidden case, blocked by every runtime
